info.title: Ryu Mail API
info.summary: Agent inboxes over HTTP, hosted or self-hosted.
info.description:
Ryu Mail stores inboxes, messages, threads, drafts and attachments, sends mail through the configured transport, and delivers signed event webhooks. One `/api/mail/*` contract has two deployments.

**Hosted Mail** (`https://api.ryuhq.com`) authenticates with an organization's node gateway key in `x-gateway-key` (minted only through Ryu node enrollment), or with a Ryu API key in `x-api-key` that carries Mail scopes: `mail:read` for reads, `mail:send` to send, reply, forward and work drafts, and `mail:manage` for inbox, domain, list, pod and webhook changes. Changing the organization mailbox, its aliases or the send policy, and deciding an approval, are console-member actions that no key can call (`x-ryu-api-key-scope: session_only`). Each hosted operation names its scope in `x-ryu-api-key-scope`. An organization key acts in its own organization; a personal key names the organization in `X-Ryu-Organization`. Either key is also limited by the current `mail.read` / `mail.manage` permissions of the member it acts for. A key without the scope gets 403 `insufficient_scope`. A signed-in console session also works from the dashboard. There is no self-serve hosted Mail signup.

**Self-hosted Mail** (`{baseUrl}`, port 7996 by default) authenticates with its own bearer token (`RYU_MAIL_API_TOKEN` on the server). One process serves one tenant.

Operations only one deployment serves are marked `x-ryu-deployment: hosted` or `x-ryu-deployment: standalone`. Schemas show the camelCase form hosted Mail returns; self-hosted Mail may use snake_case names and wrap single objects (`{ "message": … }`). The `@ryuhq/services` SDK reads both.

get.description: Upgrade to a WebSocket. Offer both `ryu-mail.v1` and `ryu-bearer.<token>` in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (on one header line or several); the server selects `ryu-mail.v1`, so the token is never echoed back. Then send a JSON `{ eventTypes?, inboxIds? }` filter. The token must be hex or URL-safe (base64url without padding), because subprotocol names allow no other characters. Offering only `ryu-bearer.<token>` (the server then echoes it) is deprecated. A token in the URL (`?token=`) is refused with 401.

post.description: Hosted Mail. Exchanges a node gateway key, a Ryu API key with `mail:read`, or a console session for a ticket that opens one `GET /api/mail/realtime` socket. Tickets are random 256-bit values, single use, valid for 30 seconds, and bound to the organization, the credential that minted them and `mail:read`. `protocols` is the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` list to offer. A credential holds at most 16 unredeemed tickets and an organization (or personal account) at most 64 (429 after that).

get.description: Hosted Mail. Upgrade to a WebSocket offering `ryu-mail.v1` and `ryu-ticket.<ticket>` in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, with a ticket from `POST /api/mail/realtime/tickets`; the server selects `ryu-mail.v1`, so the ticket is never echoed back. The first attempt consumes the ticket, whatever its outcome. Frames match self-hosted Mail: `connected` on open, a JSON `{ eventTypes?, inboxIds? }` filter acknowledged with `subscribed` (a malformed or oversized filter gets a `{ type: "error", code, error }` frame with code `invalid_subscription` instead), `ping` answered with `pong`, and `{ type: "event", event }` carrying a `MailEvent`. A node gateway key's socket sees no other node's agent inboxes. The upgrade re-checks the organization's IP allowlist against the connecting client (403 `org_ip_not_allowed`; 503 when the policy cannot be read). A credential holds at most 16 open sockets and an organization at most 64 (429). A request that is not a WebSocket upgrade gets 426 `upgrade_required`, and 503 means Mail is not configured on this deployment. Every minute an open socket re-checks the credential that minted its ticket (key or gateway credential still live with `mail:read`, member or service account still holding `mail.read`, Mail still enabled) and closes with code 4001 when it no longer may read; every socket is also closed with 4001 after 15 minutes. On 4001, mint a new ticket, reconnect, and replay any gap from `GET /api/mail/events`.

- `agent_inbox_forbidden`: A gateway key reached for another node's agent inbox; `agentId` must be `<nodeId>:<agentId>` for the key's node.

- `insufficient_scope`: The Ryu API key lacks the scope this route needs (`requiredScope`, `missingScopes`). Use a key with that scope.
- `oauth_client_not_allowed`: The organization has not allowed this OAuth app (`clientId`) to use its Mail. An owner or admin must allow it.
- `organization_mismatch`: `X-Ryu-Organization` names a different organization than the organization API key belongs to. Omit the header or send the key's own organization.
- `org_access_denied`: An organization access policy refused the request; `policyCode` says which (such as `org_ip_not_allowed` or `org_session_expired`).
- `org_ip_not_allowed`: The organization accepts realtime connections only from approved IP addresses.

reasons.description: Why the send was held: `policy_always` (the policy is `always`), `first_contact` (a recipient the alias never corresponded with), `over_recipient_cap` (more recipients than `maxRecipientsPerMessage`) or `over_new_recipient_limit` (more first contacts today than `newRecipientsPerDay`).

clientId.description: Your own id for the pod, or null.
Your own id for the pod. Creating again with the same `clientId` returns the existing pod.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the ticket expires unused.

path.description: The WebSocket path to open, relative to the Mail origin.

protocols.description: The WebSocket subprotocols to offer, in order: `ryu-mail.v1` and `ryu-ticket.<ticket>`.

ticket.description: The single-use ticket; it is spent by the first upgrade that offers it.

reason.description: Why the send was refused, up to 256 characters; recorded with the decision.

displayName.description: The sender name mail from this alias shows, up to 64 characters; quotes, angle brackets, backslashes and line breaks are removed.

attachments.description: Files to attach, each with `content` or `url`.

content_id.description: Content-ID for an inline part, referenced as `cid:` in HTML.

inline.description: Send as an inline part instead of an attachment.

url.description: Public HTTPS URL to fetch instead of `content`.

bcc.description: Blind-copy recipients. Each entry is an address or `Name <address>`.

cc.description: Copy recipients. Each entry is an address or `Name <address>`.

clientId.description: Your own id for this message. A second send from the same inbox with the same `clientId` returns the stored message instead of sending again; it is also echoed on the message.

headers.description: Extra MIME headers, by name. Hosted Mail accepts at most 64 and refuses names it sets itself; a refused name answers 400.

html.description: HTML body. Send `text`, `html` or both (or only attachments); text and HTML together may be at most 4 MiB on hosted Mail.

inReplyTo.description: The RFC 5322 `Message-ID` this message answers, for threading.

labels.description: Labels stored on the sent message (hosted Mail: at most 64, each at most 128 characters).

references.description: Space-separated Message-IDs of the conversation, oldest first, for threading.

replyTo.description: Addresses replies should go to. Each entry is an address or `Name <address>`.

subject.description: Subject line. Defaults to the original's, with `Re: ` added.

to.description: Recipients. A reply defaults to the original sender; reply-all always adds the original sender and recipients, without this inbox. Each entry is an address or `Name <address>`.

trackOpens.description: Add an open-tracking pixel to the HTML body, so a `message.opened` event fires on the first open. Ignored without `html`, and on a deployment that has not enabled open tracking.

reason.description: Why the alias was revoked, up to 256 characters; recorded on the alias.

references.description: Space-separated Message-IDs of the conversation, oldest first, for threading.

subject.description: Subject line (hosted Mail: at most 998 bytes).

to.description: Recipients; at least one. Each entry is an address or `Name <address>`.

maxRecipientsPerMessage.description: The most recipients (To, Cc and Bcc together) one send may name before it is held.

mode.description: When an agent send needs an admin's approval: never (`auto`), for a first contact (`first_contact`), or every time (`always`).

newRecipientsPerDay.description: The most first-contact recipients an alias may write to in a day before a send is held.

preApprovedDomains.description: Recipients on these domains never count as a first contact.

aliasId.description: The alias override to set; null or absent sets the owner default.

maxRecipientsPerMessage.description: The most recipients (To, Cc and Bcc together) one send may name before it is held, 1 to 100. Omitted keeps the stored value, or 10 on a new row.

mode.description: When an agent send needs an admin's approval: never (`auto`), for a first contact (`first_contact`), or every time (`always`). The recipient and first-contact limits apply in every mode.

newRecipientsPerDay.description: The most first-contact recipients an alias may write to in a day before a send is held, 0 to 10000. Omitted keeps the stored value, or 20 on a new row.

preApprovedDomains.description: Domain names; a leading `@` is dropped.

url.description: A short-lived signed download URL. Fetch it without Mail credentials.

configured.description: Whether Mail is configured on this deployment.

domain.description: The domain hosted inboxes use; null when unset.

inboxCount.description: How many inboxes exist, where the deployment reports it.

sendConfigured.description: Whether a sending transport is configured.

latestMessage.description: The newest message of the thread (a MailMessage), or null.

messageCount.description: How many messages the thread holds.

participants.description: Addresses that sent or received mail in the thread.

subject.description: The thread's subject; null when it has none.

addLabels.description: Labels to add to every message of the thread.

removeLabels.description: Labels to remove from every message of the thread.

agentId.description: The agent that receives the alias, as `<nodeId>:<agentId>`. It inherits every account bound to the address.

confirmAddress.description: The exact address of the alias.

description.description: Hosted Mail: a note about the inbox; an empty string clears it. Self-hosted Mail ignores it.

metadata.description: Self-hosted Mail: replaces your key-value data. Hosted Mail ignores it on update.

podId.description: Move the inbox into this pod. On hosted Mail `null` takes it out; self-hosted Mail treats `null` as no change.

rotateWebhookSecret.description: Replace the inbox webhook's signing secret; the response returns it once.

webhookUrl.description: Hosted Mail: set the inbox webhook URL; an empty string removes it. Self-hosted Mail ignores it.

aliasClaimPolicy.description: Who may claim an alias: `agents` claim on their own, `approval` waits for an admin, `admins_only` is admin assignment only.

brandingRemoved.description: Removing the Ryu branding needs a Plus, Pro, Max or Teams plan.

enabled.description: Whether the mailbox sends and receives mail.

name.description: The mailbox's display name, up to 128 characters.

used.description: Pending and active aliases, plus legacy agent inboxes; revoked aliases do not count.

freeBaseline.description: True when the owner is on the free baseline rather than a paid plan or contract.

inboxLimit.description: Primary mailboxes and shared inboxes allowed; null for unlimited.

monthlySendLimit.description: Sends allowed per month; null for unlimited.

monthlySendsUsed.description: Sends counted so far this month.

storageLimitBytes.description: Storage allowed, in bytes; null for unlimited.

allowance.description: What the plan or contract allows, and this month's sends.

code.description: The extracted code; null when the message holds only a link.

link.description: The extracted link, dropped when longer than 512 characters; null when none.

messageId.description: The message the code came from.

codes.description: Codes and links found in the agent's 20 newest matching messages, newest first.

clientId.description: Your own id for the webhook, or null.

enabled.description: Whether deliveries are sent; `false` while paused.

headers.description: Names of the custom headers; values are write-only.

inboxIds.description: Deliver only events of these inboxes; empty for no inbox filter.

podIds.description: Deliver only events of inboxes in these pods; empty for no pod filter.

signatureScheme.description: `standard`: Standard Webhooks signatures. `legacy`: a webhook created before them, whose `svix-signature` is keyed with the UTF-8 bytes of the whole secret.

url.description: The HTTPS endpoint events are POSTed to.

clientId.description: Your own id for the webhook. Creating again with the same `clientId` returns the existing webhook.

eventTypes.description: Events to deliver, such as `message.received`, `message.sent`, `message.delivered`, `message.bounced`, `message.complained`, `message.rejected` or `message.opened`. Omit for the standard set; an empty list answers 400.

headers.description: Custom headers sent with every delivery. Values are write-only, and names Mail sets itself (`webhook-*`, `svix-*`, `host`, `cookie`, `content-length`) are refused.

inboxIds.description: Deliver only events of these inboxes.

podIds.description: Deliver only events of inboxes in these pods.

url.description: Public HTTPS endpoint. Loopback, private, link-local and metadata targets are refused.

deliveredAt.description: When an attempt succeeded; null until then.

lastError.description: Why the last attempt failed; null when none failed.

headers.description: Custom headers to add or overwrite, by name.

removeHeaders.description: Names of custom headers to remove.

data.description: The event's fields. Message events carry `message` (`id` is what `GET /api/mail/messages/{id}` reads, `message_id` the RFC `Message-ID`); `message.received` includes the full body.

event_id.description: The event id; equals `webhook-id`. Deduplicate on it.

clientId.description: Your own id for the webhook. Creating again with the same `clientId` returns the existing webhook.

eventTypes.description: Events to deliver, such as `message.received`, `message.sent`, `message.delivered`, `message.bounced`, `message.complained`, `message.rejected` or `message.opened`. Omit for the standard set; an empty list answers 400.

headers.description: Custom headers sent with every delivery. Values are write-only, and names Mail sets itself (`webhook-*`, `svix-*`, `host`, `cookie`, `content-length`) are refused.

inboxIds.description: Deliver only events of these inboxes.

podIds.description: Deliver only events of inboxes in these pods.

url.description: Public HTTPS endpoint. Loopback, private, link-local and metadata targets are refused.

addInboxIds.description: Add inboxes to the scope without replacing it.

addPodIds.description: Add pods to the scope without replacing it.

removeHeaders.description: Names of custom headers to remove.

rotateSecret.description: Replace the signing secret; the response carries it once.

secret.description: The `whsec_` signing secret, returned only when it is minted or rotated.
